threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’re still avoiding the bus stop at Kingsland Road during rush hour. Locals know it’s a game of survival, not a commute.
Last week, a bloke on the 35 serenaded the whole bus with a broken ukulele. I swear half of us joined in for the chorus of 'Wonderwall'—only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Walking past the Turkish bakery on Sonnenallee, the smell of fresh simit made me realize this place has a heartbeat all its own.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner while listening to a spontaneous street concert—just a regular Tuesday night, nothing planned.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they know to  avoid the BART escalators during rush hour; the real ones just take the stairs and breathe through it.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a three-piece suit arguing with a raccoon over a burrito on the 14. Muni truly captures the spirit of this city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's squares are just for selfies, but locals use them for evening chats over vermut, not just snapshots.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their habit of hesitating at every intersection, glancing at their phone like it's a treasure map instead of just asking for directions.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the ‘bus replacement’ signs pop up, like it’s some sort of foreign language. Welcome to the chaos!
Last night on the 133, a chap serenaded the whole bus with Adele. The driver couldn't help but chuckle, it felt like a mini concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard someone debating the best falafel spot while waiting for the bus at Hermannplatz. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous street party erupting next to a traditional Turkish kebab shop. No planning, just music and a crowd.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name all the taquerias on the same block without breaking a sweat. It’s not just about the food; it's the stories tied to each place.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 at 5 PM, and a guy was singing opera like he was in the Met. Everyone just vibed with it—only in San Francisco!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they’ve seen Gràcia by visiting Park Güell, but they miss the real charm in the small squares where locals gather for vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their hesitance to try the local bakeries; they're still clutching those giant pre-packaged snacks.
